overall_summary: Analysis of deduplicated YouTube Shorts data reveals that extreme cosmic scenarios, counter-intuitive planetary physics, and immersive 'What If' thought experiments dominate both absolute views and engagement efficiency (likes-per-view). Specifically, topics involving exotic exoplanets, extreme environments, and interactive existential scenarios (e.g., falling into unusual planets) outperform general abstract science or biology facts. Engagement is heavily concentrated on high-stakes visual hooks delivered within 19-21 seconds.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,031 views, 36 likes) outperform standard static space facts by a factor of 3-5x.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on surreal, high-contrast astronomical phenomenons framed as immersive physical scenarios or extreme hypothetical choices.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (725 views, 25 likes) demonstrate that bizarre planetary mechanics and extreme weather hooks yield exceptionally high engagement ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Continue utilizing shocking superlatives and paradoxes in titles, ensuring the visual payoff matches the linguistic hook.

weak_patterns.pattern: Low-Stakes Biological or Psychological Facts Without Visual Contrast
weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) suffer from very low traction compared to space and planetary content.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract internal biology/psychology unless paired with a highly cinematic, bizarre visual narrative or high-stakes physical consequence.

weak_patterns.evidence: 12-15 second videos (e.g., Octopuses Have Three Hearts variants) show lower sustained momentum and shallower engagement depth compared to the 19-21 second format which allows proper setup, twist, and resolution.
weak_patterns.action: Standardize runtime strictly between 19 and 21 seconds to maximize loop potential and algorithmic dwell time.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into a Star Made Entirely of Neon?
next_video.opening_direction: Start with a mesmerizing, neon-glowing orb suspended in deep space, asking the viewer what happens if gravity pulls them past the glowing outer layers.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that instead of burning instantly, you would experience a surreal, luminescent freefall through glowing plasma before extreme pressure seals your fate.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the proven high-performing 'What If' planetary/stellar fall format while introducing a novel celestial body (neon star) distinct from previously covered diamond, ice, or dark planets.
fresh_topic_constraints: Must not feature diamonds, liquid metal, glass rain, or black planets.
Must feature a newly introduced astronomical element (neon star/plasma mechanics).
Must maintain strict factual grounding in astrophysics.

experiment: Test if replacing standard declarative space fact titles with second-person experiential 'What If' immersion prompts increases initial 3-second retention by at least 15%.
